run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T02:01:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend is firing because the product-catalog workload is down: Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog was rolled out at 2026-11-17T02:00:02Z with a container command override of ["invalid-command"] on an unchanged image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog). The new pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l never starts (OCI runtime error exec "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH, last termination StartError, 5 restarts, BackOff) and the old pod was deleted at 02:00:11Z, leaving Service product-catalog with zero ready endpoints. The resulting span-level error burst on frontend begins between 02:00:53Z and 02:01:53Z (frontend error spans were exactly zero in every earlier sample of the window) and is concentrated on operations that require product-catalog: frontend GET /api/products/{productId} 2451.2 and its outbound grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client span 2451.2, plus downstream-amplified GET /api/recommendations 468.27 and POST /api/checkout 312.69. The same dependency failure appears in recommendation (/oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts 471.47) and checkout (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 292.27), and frontend-proxy records 3473.32 ingress error spans carrying the resulting failures. The frontend process itself was not the failing component: its pod is ready with 0 restarts and its non-product-catalog routes show zero errors. Flag-injection flags are all off, and no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota objects exist in the namespace. A fraud-detection OOMKill/restart at ~01:50:05Z is a separate change that preceded the error onset and shows no error spans of its own.

claims.text: Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog reports status.readyReplicas null and availableReplicas null, and its pod template container 'product-catalog' sets command ["invalid-command"] on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog.

Two ReplicaSets belong to Deployment product-catalog: product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 01:30:01Z, replicas 0, no command override) and product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 02:00:02Z, replicas 1, command ["invalid-command"]); both use the same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog, so this rollout is a configuration-only change.

Events in otel-demo record the failing start and rollout: Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l 'Error: failed to create containerd task: ... exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH' x6 (Warning, 02:00:23Z-02:03:32Z) and BackOff x25 (02:00:24Z-02:05:34Z); Deployment product-catalog ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-fcf7564cf from 0 to 1' at 02:00:02Z and 'Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0' at 02:00:11Z.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf) is phase Running with ready=false, restartCount 5 and last termination reason StartError, started 2026-11-17T02:00:19Z.

Endpoints object product-catalog has one subset with zero ready addresses and one notReadyAddress (100.96.2.148), so Service product-catalog (selector opentelemetry.io/name=product-catalog) routes to no ready backend.

product-catalog span volume decayed to zero right after the rollout: the 5m increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=product-catalog went 3281.11 (02:00:53Z), 2563.33, 1756.67, 962.22, 102.22, then 0 at 02:05:53Z and every later sample.

frontend recorded no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans before the change and an error burst after it: the 5m increase of frontend error spans was 0 at 02:00:53Z, then 516.67, 2427.47, 4041.61, 5623.47, 6648.89, 6751.93, 6755.56, 6564.44, 6967.18 and 5305.27 at 02:01:53Z onward.

Over the 4173s window the frontend error spans are concentrated on product-catalog-dependent operations by span_name: GET /api/products/{productId} 2451.2, GET /api/recommendations 468.27, POST /api/checkout 312.69, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 312.79, and the outbound client spans grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 2451.2, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations 468.27, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 312.79, tcp.connect 17.32.

The same product-catalog dependency failure appears in other services' own error spans over the window: recommendation /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts 471.47 and get_product_list 471.47; checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 292.27 and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 292.27; frontend-proxy ingress 3473.32 and 'router frontend egress' 3460.08.

frontend's own process was not the failing component: Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 is Running with ready=true and restarts 0, and within the frontend error series the routes that do not need product-catalog stayed at 0 errors (GET /api/cart 0, POST /api/cart 0, GET /api/data 0) while product-catalog-dependent routes failed.

cart kept serving with normal span volume throughout the burst (5m call volume 3690-4994 spans at 02:01:53Z-02:09:53Z), and the per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase query returned no cart series, so the cart path was not the failing dependency.

Cluster-side plumbing was clean in the namespace: otel-demo contains no NetworkPolicy objects and no ResourceQuota objects, so traffic blocking or quota exhaustion is not what left product-catalog without a ready backend.

The demo fault-injection flag productCatalogFailure was considered and rejected: ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) has every flag, including productCatalogFailure and paymentFailure, with defaultVariant "off", and the observed failure is a container exec failure before any application logic runs.

A crash or restart of the frontend deployment was considered as the cause and rejected: the frontend pod shows restarts 0 and no terminated container state, and the frontend error burst starts only after the product-catalog rollout, on operations that require product-catalog.

Changed during the window for another reason: Pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-8bpr4 was OOMKilled and restarted (restartCount 1, lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled, container recreated 01:50:05Z), roughly ten minutes before the frontend error onset between 02:00:53Z and 02:01:53Z, and the per-service error query returned no fraud-detection error series.

The span-volume drop to zero for accounting, currency, email, shipping, quote, payment and fraud-detection (each at 0 spans/5m by 02:05:53Z) is likely a traffic consequence rather than their own failure: checkout's pod template declares CURRENCY_ADDR, EMAIL_ADDR, PAYMENT_ADDR and SHIPPING_ADDR dependencies, checkout's PlaceOrder already fails at oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, and the per-service error query returned no error series for those services.

The alert's reported magnitude (current 16.8667) is consistent with frontend error-span throughput after the product-catalog change: the last 5m increase of frontend error spans was 5305.27 at 02:10:53Z, about 17.7 spans per second.

Remove the command override from Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog so the container runs the image default entrypoint (as ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc did with no command), then confirm a ready pod and a populated ready-address list for Service product-catalog before treating the alert as resolved.
Audit who patched the product-catalog pod template at 02:00:02Z via cluster audit logs or an integrated change-history source, since the actor is not visible in the objects returned by this Run.

gaps: Change history is not integrated (data_sources.not_integrated: change_history), so who or what applied command ["invalid-command"] to Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog cannot be verified; managedFields are not present in the objects returned.

Jaeger trace retrieval returned no_data for service frontend (01:50:00Z-02:00:00Z and 02:01:00Z-02:11:26Z, also with tag error=true) and for service product-catalog (01:50:00Z-02:11:26Z), so the raw span error text/status detail of the failed product-catalog calls (for example a gRPC UNAVAILABLE message) was not observed; only span-metric status codes and operation names are available.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready, kube_pod_container_info) returned no_data, and no {__name__=~"kube_.*"} names were listed, so the readiness timeline rests on events plus current pod/endpoint state rather than a metric series over time.

Pod logs were not obtainable: fetch_pod_logs for product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l returned no_data (0 lines current, previous instance unavailable) and for frontend-675fd7b5c5-9f6l5 returned no_data (0 lines read in 01:55:00Z-02:11:26Z), so frontend's own log-level error text and product-catalog's startup output are unknown.

Error status of cart, currency, email, shipping, quote, payment, image-provider and kafka is only weakly covered: the per-service STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase query returned no series for them, which shows the query matched nothing, not a measured zero error rate.
Alertmanager's own recording/alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not found: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no_data.
next_steps: Revert or correct the product-catalog Deployment pod template command, then confirm the pod becomes ready and Service product-catalog gains a ready endpoint.
Review cluster audit logs or GitOps history for the product-catalog Deployment change at 2026-11-17T02:00:02Z to identify the actor and prevent recurrence.

After product-catalog recovers, re-check frontend error spans for GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations and POST /api/checkout, plus frontend-proxy ingress errors, and verify the downstream services (accounting, currency, email, shipping, quote, payment, fraud-detection) resume span volume.
Investigate the fraud-detection OOMKill (restart at ~01:50:05Z, memory limit 400Mi) as an unrelated reliability item.
